title_lines: 美国页岩油却不敢增产
title_highlights: 美国页岩油却不敢增产

subtitles.en: Well, you know, interestingly enough, when oil is at $60, $65, we were seeing the record of U.S. production. I was quite perplexed by that. Right now at $95, $100, a barrel of pollen, certainly prices are high enough. Now, they're high enough, but are they going to remain high?
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，当油价在60-65美元时，美国产量创纪录，我当时很困惑。现在95-100美元，价格确实够高，但能维持吗？

subtitles.en: We are seeing some hints, particularly when we look at the CFTC data, they're commitment to trader's reports. When we look at the disaggregated portion of that report that serves as a proxy for E&P hedgers, then we're seeing a significant amount of futures markets sold forward.
subtitles.zh: 我们看到一些迹象，特别是CFTC持仓报告。在分项数据中，作为勘探生产商对冲代理的部分，我们看到大量期货被提前卖出。

subtitles.en: So what we can say with confidence is that E&P producers are selling this conflict. Now, the question is, are they selling it? And then they're going to meet that with future production, which would be the implication. We have to admit that remains to be seen.
subtitles.zh: 我们可以肯定的是，勘探生产商正在利用冲突溢价卖出。问题是他们是否会以未来产量来兑现，这还有待观察。

subtitles.en: But typically, the knock on is you'd want to see months of a new pricing regime that we are in, rather than just a kind of a short live. Okay, this is a market, a futures market that is trading with every whim, every social media post that comes out there. That's not a fundamental physical plan right now.
subtitles.zh: 但通常，你需要看到新价格机制持续数月，而不是短暂现象。目前期货市场受情绪和社交媒体影响，这不是基于基本面现货的计划。

subtitles.en: So we do know that is, again, I'll reiterate that a lot of oil has been sold forward by the producer class. Now, that could be a speculative hedge, it could be, but it's not. So the likelihood is we will start to see production ramp up to meet this.
subtitles.zh: 我们确实知道，生产商已经卖出了大量远期原油。这可能是一种投机性对冲，但并非如此。因此，我们很可能会看到产量增加以满足需求。

subtitles.en: But the question is, can we get that production from where it is, who needs to be in the amount of time that we need, and that is, the answer to that is no. So from a longer term perspective, we might see, the indications are there, but will it make enough of a difference to impact price without other factors being addressed for this summer unlikely now?
subtitles.zh: 但问题是，我们能否在需要的时间内将产量提升到所需水平？答案是否定的。从长期看，有迹象表明产量会增加，但能否足以影响今夏价格，而不解决其他因素？目前不太可能。

subtitles.en: The price of airfare can rise. Cheap flights can also exist, but that doesn't necessarily mean that that is working for airlines.
subtitles.zh: 机票价格可能上涨，廉价航班也可能存在，但这并不一定意味着对航司有利。

subtitles.en: Airlines are really feeling the pressure from this additional cost, and they're looking at ways to protect their margins. So they're really looking to be creative here.
subtitles.zh: 航司正感受到额外成本的压力，他们正在想办法保护利润空间，所以会寻求一些创新做法。

subtitles.en: And one of such ways is looking at ancillaries like bag fees. And it's sort of a win-win for the airlines in this stage because, yes, they're getting extra revenue from these increased bag fees.
subtitles.zh: 其中一种方式就是行李费这类附加服务。现阶段对航司来说算是双赢，因为他们确实从提高的行李费中获得了额外收入。

subtitles.en: But then they're also not subject to a 7.5 excise tax that they put on base fares that they are subject to. So that's more money in the pocket, as well as they have now this framing, this justification of higher jet fuel prices.
subtitles.zh: 而且行李费还不用缴纳基础票价需缴纳的7.5%消费税，这样他们能留下更多收入，同时还能以油价上涨为由头。

subtitles.en: And they can always push back and say, you know what, you don't have to check a bag even though the prices have risen. But do travelers, can they just decide not to check a bag?
subtitles.zh: 他们总是可以反驳说，即使价格上涨，你也可以选择不托运行李。但旅客们真的能决定不托运吗？
en_highlights: don't have to check a bag

subtitles.en: We asked that question for families that, unfortunately, are feeling the pressure of having or needing to check a bag. So it's really a win-win for the airlines, and they lose, lose for travelers, especially when, yes, base fares have increased domestic prices for summer.
subtitles.zh: 我们向那些不得不托运行李的家庭提出了这个问题。所以这对航司来说是双赢，对旅客来说则是双重损失，尤其是夏季国内基础票价已经上涨。

subtitles.en: Just for example, according to our Going data, up 18% international fares, up 7.5%. So unfortunately, this summer specifically is really going to be challenging for that cost-conscious traveler.
subtitles.zh: 根据我们的Going数据，国际票价上涨18%，国内上涨7.5%。所以不幸的是，今年夏天对注重成本的旅客来说将尤其具有挑战性。

subtitles.en: I'm starting to get very mad at David Gura who was taking his vacation now, and it's partly already planned this, whereas I was waiting to the end of summer. And the shoulder season is a good deal.
subtitles.zh: 我开始对David Gura很生气，他现在就去度假了，而且早就计划好了，而我还在等夏末。淡季出行其实很划算。

subtitles.en: But my concern is that when we see industries raise these prices, they don't tend to go back down, because consumers get used to it that threshold sticks. We very rarely if oil prices go down or see those other prices go back down.
subtitles.zh: 但我担心的是，一旦行业提高这些价格，它们往往不会回落，因为消费者会习惯，这个门槛就固定了。即使油价下跌，我们也很少看到其他价格回落。
en_highlights: don't tend to go back down

subtitles.en: Do you think these increased bag fees will stay at this level? I really hope I'm wrong, but I am not a betting woman, but I would bet that these fees are here to stay.
subtitles.zh: 你觉得这些提高的行李费会维持在这个水平吗？我真希望我错了，但我不爱打赌，不过我愿意打赌这些费用会持续下去。

subtitles.en: They're pretty sticky historically. We have seen bag fees risen every few years. And it's likely that this was in airline's playbook all along, but we have this perfect time frame now to raise fees and have a justification to do so.
subtitles.zh: 从历史上看，它们相当顽固。我们看到行李费每隔几年就会上涨。这很可能一直是航司的既定策略，只是现在正好有合适的时机和理由来涨价。

subtitles.en: As well as, you know, JetBlue really started the trend and then United joined. And if you noticed, it's a herd mentality. You know, if one airline does it, it's a green light for everybody else. And unfortunately again, travelers are looking at this to be the new norm.
subtitles.zh: 而且，捷蓝航空开了先河，美联航跟进。如果你注意到了，这就是一种跟风心态。一家航司这么做，就等于给其他航司开了绿灯。不幸的是，旅客们不得不把这视为新常态。

subtitles.en: Is it a way to creatively get us to buy sort of that more expensive tier of ticket too? Because if you think about it from, you know, the perspective of these airlines, they have these different tiers of service. So even the big three are have these basic economy fares to try to compete with the ultra low cost carriers.
subtitles.zh: 这是不是一种巧妙的方式，让我们去买更贵的舱位？因为从航司的角度看，他们有不同的服务等级。甚至三大航也推出基础经济舱来与超低成本航司竞争。

subtitles.en: So if you're in basic economy, maybe you don't get, you know, to choose a seat or to check a bag, you have to pay to check a bag. But then if you buy that one tier higher, you can get some of those things and maybe those margins are better.
subtitles.zh: 所以如果你买基础经济舱，可能不能选座或免费托运行李，托运要付费。但如果你买高一级的舱位，就能享受这些服务，航司的利润也可能更好。

subtitles.en: Yeah, it's unfortunately feeling like you are being punished for just trying to get a base fare. We call basic economy, just the base fare. It is basically just a seat at this point. And so we want travelers not to feel like there are no options because actually there are options when you do buy up.
subtitles.zh: 是的，不幸的是，感觉就像你只是想买基础票价却受到了惩罚。我们把基础经济舱称为基础票价，它基本上只是一个座位。所以我们希望旅客不要觉得没有选择，因为当你升级舱位时，其实是有选择的。

subtitles.en: You are giving yourself the flexibility of taking advantage of price drops when and if they occur. And that is one huge tip that we would impart on anybody that is looking to fly in the near future that's worried about higher costs, especially for summer.
subtitles.zh: 你给了自己利用价格下跌的灵活性，如果价格下跌的话。这是我们要给所有近期打算乘机、担心成本上升的人的一个重要建议，尤其是夏季出行。

subtitles.en: When you book that main economy fare, you have the flexibility to take advantage of a notification when it comes in, whether it's on Google flights, whatever tracking you have, maybe it's on the Going app, call the airlines, they reprice you, and then you get a credit for the difference to use in the future within the year. So you're never actually losing out when you book that higher fare class.
subtitles.zh: 当你预订标准经济舱时，你可以利用价格提醒，比如Google Flights或Going应用上的追踪，然后致电航司，他们会重新定价，你就能获得差价积分，在一年内使用。所以预订更高舱位时，你实际上不会亏。

subtitles.en: However, yes, it is a more expensive ticket on the upfront.
subtitles.zh: 不过，是的，前期票价确实更贵。

clips.title: 旅行专家Katy Nastro：邮轮也有隐藏费用？家庭出行需留意
title_lines: 邮轮也有隐藏费用？家庭出行需留意
合同条款暗藏额外收费

subtitles.en: All right, before we let you go, it's not just flights. This is impacting cruises as well.
subtitles.zh: 好的，在结束之前，不只是机票，邮轮也受到了影响。

subtitles.en: Cruises are like the family bargain basement travel. I have so many friends who describe themselves as being really not cruise people, but then they need to do a vacation with tiny children and older parents and families who can't decide and they've all gone on a cruise and said, you know what, it was perfect, but it was affordable. It makes sense that people are looking at alternatives.
subtitles.zh: 邮轮就像是家庭的经济型旅行。我有很多朋友自称不是邮轮爱好者，但当他们需要带着小孩和老人一起度假，或者家人难以决定时，他们都选择了邮轮，并说“很完美，而且负担得起”。人们寻找替代方案是有道理的。

subtitles.en: We are looking at all-inclusive, domestic all-inclusive, Vegas just announced. Some of that is being implemented. Cruises always a family favorite because you know what your bottom line cost is going to be.
subtitles.zh: 我们也在关注全包式度假，国内全包式，拉斯维加斯刚刚宣布。有些已经在实施。邮轮一直是家庭的最爱，因为你知道总成本是多少。

subtitles.en: However, written into cruise contracts is little stipulations surrounding that there may be fees after the fact, even after you paid. Now, it varies across cruise lines, but that's something that travelers really need to be aware of.
subtitles.zh: 然而，邮轮合同中有些小条款规定，即使在付款后，也可能产生额外费用。不同邮轮公司规定不同，但旅客真的需要留意这一点。

subtitles.en: And unfortunately, again, it's looking to be a challenge for those cost-conscious travelers this year, specifically families.
subtitles.zh: 不幸的是，这对今年注重成本的旅客来说又是一个挑战，尤其是家庭。
